drivingQuestion: How far does the mishna's dispute over a miscarriage lacking human form extend?
outcomeNote: A single amoraic statement scoping the mishna's dispute; no challenge follows in this unit.

segments.he: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: כֹּל שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ כּוּ׳. אָמַר רַב יִרְמְיָה בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַב: הַכֹּל מוֹדִים: גּוּפוֹ תַּיִישׁ וּפָנָיו אָדָם — אָדָם, גּוּפוֹ אָדָם וּפָנָיו תַּיִישׁ — וְלֹא כְלוּם.
segments.en: § The mishna teaches: «And the Rabbis say: Any» discharged entity «that is not» of human form does not render the woman impure. «Rav Yirmeya bar Abba says» that «Rav says: All concede» that if a woman discharged an entity «whose body is» that of «a goat and whose face is» that of «a human,» it is considered «a human» offspring, i.e., even the Rabbis rule that the woman is impure in this case. Likewise, if «its body is» that of «a human and its face is» that of «a goat,» Rabbi Meir concedes that «it is nothing,» and the woman is pure.

moves.summary: The gemara quotes the Rabbis' clause of the mishna.

moves.cueHe: אמר רב ירמיה בר אבא אמר רב: הכל מודים
moves.summary: Rav (via Rav Yirmeya bar Abba) rules that all concede in the goat-body/human-face and human-body/goat-face cases.
moves.about: Rav's statement that all concede in the goat/human cases

edges.cueHe: וחכמים אומרים: כל שאין בו כו׳
edges.about: quotes the Rabbis' clause of the mishna as the lemma for discussion
whether a miscarried entity without human form renders the woman impure with the impurity of childbirth

edges.cueHe: אמר רב ירמיה בר אבא אמר רב
edges.about: Rav's statement that all concede in the goat/human cases
the mishna's dispute does not extend to a goat body with human face (human) or human body with goat face (nothing); the face decides for all

positions.claim: an entity lacking human form is not a child and does not render the woman impure
all agree: goat body with human face is human; human body with goat face is nothing
